body.p: Claims 1-17 and 19-20 are pending in the present application. Claims 1 and 3 are
amended in this paper. No claims are canceled in this paper. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not

necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications.

A telephonic interview regarding the instant matter was conducted on May 11, 2023 between Examiner Curry and Applicant's representative, Micah Drayton, Reg # 69,906, and Alexander Bost. Patentability under 35 U.S.C. § 103 was discussed in light of proposed claim amendments. Applicant thanks the Examiner for her time and consideration in conducting the interview. No agreement was reached.
Epstein/Glaser/James
Claims 1, 6-11, 13-17, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly

unpatentable over Epstein et al. (US 2015/0344143), hereinafter Epstein in view of Glaser et al. (US 2011/0042520), hereinafter Glaser, in further view of Rick James (pilotteacher.com NPL reference), hereinafter James. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claim 1
Claim 1 as amended recites:
A method for fueling and using an aircraft, wherein the method
comprises:
storing, using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an
airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe,
liquified gas fuel;
fueling, using a fuel line, an aircraft, wherein fueling further
comprises:
filling the fuel tank with liquified gas fuel to a desired level, wherein
the desired level comprises fuel for a plurality of flights plus
reserves, wherein a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related to the fuel tank, wherein the
sensor converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a
signal that is then transmitted to a computing device; and
removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of
the desired level in the aircraft; and
preparing the fuel tank for flight as a function of the desired level;
and
flying, using the aircraft, a plurality of flights using the liquid gas
fuel.

The Office asserts that Epstein teaches "storing, using a fuel tank, liquified gas fuel" in Fig. 3 and P. [0021]-[0022]. However, the above-described language of Epstein does not teach, suggest, or motivate using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1. Applicant asserts that Epstein does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein.

Glaser fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein. Glaser is not asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1. Applicant asserts that Glaser does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, Applicant submits that claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination. Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination.

James fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein and Glaser. James is not asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1. Applicant asserts that James does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe."

Further, The Office takes Official Notice that "it is well known to fill tanks to a desired level and that the amount of fuel for more than one flight plus reserves." MPEP 2144.03(A) states "It would not be appropriate for the examiner to take official notice of facts without citing a prior art reference where the facts asserted to be well known are not beyond dispute, or are not capable of instant and unquestionable demonstration as being well-known." [Applicant's emphasis partially added.] Applicant respectfully traverses the Official Notice. The James reference on page 2, paragraph 2 contradicts The Office's assertion, reciting "All planes are fuelled for the next flight only." Accordingly, Applicant submits that the facts asserted by The Office to be well known are not beyond dispute and respectfully requests withdrawal of the Official Notice asserted by The Office.

Further, The Office asserts that the motivation to combine the reference of Epstein with the reference of James for the purposes of teaching "fueling, over a time period of time exceeding 30 minutes" would be to "be efficient including turnaround time to make money." (Office Action, p. 3.) However, Applicant notes that the motivation asserted by The Office would encourage one of ordinary skill in the art to pursue precisely the opposite action than ensuring a fueling time was above a threshold as previously claimed. Moreover, because the relevant limitation has been removed from the claim, Applicant respectfully asserts that the James reference does not teach, suggest, or motivate claim 1 as amended.

Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, Applicant submits that claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.
Each of claims 6-11, 13-17, and 20 depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As

noted above, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 6-11, 13-17, and 20 as amended are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least their dependency on patentably distinguishable claim 1. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of these rejections.
Epstein/Glaser/James/D'Auvergne

Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, Glaser, and James as applied to claim 1 above, respectively, and in further view of D'Auvergne (US 7,281,682), hereinafter D'Auvergne. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 2 depends directly from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is patentably

distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 2 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

D'Auvergne fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein, Glaser, and James. D'Auvergne is not asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1. Applicant asserts that D'Auvergne does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and D'Auvergne, alone or in combination. Accordingly, claim 2 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and D'Auvergne, alone or in combination, for at least its dependence on patentably distinguishable claim 1. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.
Epstein/Glaser/James/Wexler

Claims 3 and 5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, Glaser, and James as applied to claim 1 above, respectively, and in further view of Wexler et al. (US 6,123,295), hereinafter Wexler. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claims 3 and 5 depend directly or indirectly from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is
patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3 and 5 are
patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Wexler fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein, Glaser, and James. Wexler is not asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim

1. Applicant asserts that Wexler does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or in combination. Accordingly, claims 3 and 5 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or in combination, for at least their dependence on patentably distinguishable claim 1.
Further, claim 3 has been amended to recite "wherein the fuel tank is configured to have a multi-lobe geometry and comprises an insulation material with a thermal conductivity less than

0.10 W/m-K." The Office has not asserted that Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or in combination, teach, suggest, or motivate "wherein the fuel tank is configured to have a multi- lobe geometry and comprises an insulation material with a thermal conductivity less than 0.10 W/m-K" as recited by amended claim 3. Applicant asserts that Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or in combination, do not teach, suggest, or motivate "wherein the fuel tank is configured to have a multi-lobe geometry and comprises an insulation material with a thermal conductivity less than 0.10 W/m-K." Accordingly, claims 3 and 5 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or in combination, for at least this reason. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of these rejections.
Epstein/Glaser/James/Wexler/Clark

Claim 4 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler as applied to claim 3 above, and in further view of Clark et al. (US 6,123,295), hereinafter Clark. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 4 depends indirectly from claim 1 and directly from claim 3. As noted above,
claims 1 and 3 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or

in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 4 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Clark fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein, Glaser, James, and Wexler. Clark is not asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1 or "wherein the fuel tank is configured to have a multi-lobe geometry and comprises an insulation material with a thermal conductivity less than 0.10 W/m-K" as recited by amended claim 3. Applicant asserts that Clark does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" or "wherein the fuel tank is configured to have a multi-lobe geometry and comprises an insulation material with a thermal conductivity less than 0.10 W/m-K." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claims 1 and 3 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, Wexler, and Clark, alone or in combination. Accordingly, claim 4 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, Wexler, and Clark, alone or in combination, for at least its dependence on patentably distinguishable claim 1 and claim 3. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.
Epstein/Glaser/James/Clark

Claim 19 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, Glaser, and James as applied to claim 1 above, respectively, and in further view of Clark et al. (US 6,123,295), hereinafter Clark. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 19 depends directly from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is patentably

distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 19 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Clark fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein, Glaser, and James. Clark is not asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an

airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1. Applicant asserts that Clark does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Clark, alone or in combination. Accordingly, claim 19 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Clark, alone or in combination, for at least its dependence on patentably distinguishable claim 1. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.
Epstein/Glaser/James/Benassi

Claim 12 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein, Glaser, and James as applied to claim 1 above, respectively, and in further view of Benassi et al. (US 2012/0119032), hereinafter Benassi. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 12 depends indirectly from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is patentably

distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 12 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, and James, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above and its dependence on patentably distinguishable claim 1.
Benassi fails to cure the deficiencies of Epstein, Glaser, and James. Benassi is not

asserted by The Office to teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe" as recited by amended claim 1. Applicant asserts that Benassi does not teach, suggest, or motivate "using a fuel tank that provides structural support to an airframe of the aircraft and carries shear loads from the airframe." Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Benassi, alone or in combination. Claim 12 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Glaser, James, and Benassi, alone or in combination, for at least its dependence on patentably distinguishable claim 1. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.

Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a condition for allowance and respectfully solicits the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted, /Micah Drayton/
